source.title: BOTANIC-0: a series of foundation models for plant genomic data
source.citation: Jean Ogier du Terrail et al., 2026
source.authors: Jean Ogier du Terrail; Tanguy Marchand; V. Cabeli; Zhor Khadir; C. Véran; Léonard Strouk

record.tranche_reason: Tests loss and downstream-performance scaling in plant genomic language models, an extension to genomic data rather than natural-text language models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports pretraining-loss trends in Figure 1 and downstream probing results across pretraining checkpoints in Figure 4. These are relevant results. It does not fit or report power-law exponents, make small-run forecasts, or evaluate compute-optimal allocations. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Three plant genomic MLM models (114M, 260M, 991M) are trained, and held-out loss and downstream probing are reported across model size and pretraining steps. This is a new setting (DNA, not text), so it bears on V5 and V6. No power law is fitted, so only the direction of scaling is tested, not its form.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say MLM loss improved with model size and training duration, hinting at scaling laws that need further study before larger-scale performance can be forecast. They also say no plateau was seen with model size, and that frozen-embedding downstream performance improved with capacity and training time. They note downstream curves vs steps are less smooth and less monotonic than loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses masked language modeling on plant DNA with 6-mer tokens; it follows the AgroNT genomic-model pipeline rather than reproducing the original natural-text autoregressive scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes MLM batch construction is stochastic and loss is estimated; downstream probing curves are less smooth and monotonic than pretraining loss.
record.problems: Only three model sizes are compared; loss results are plotted rather than numerically tabulated, no power-law fits or uncertainty estimates are reported, and no parameters/tokens/compute or fixed-compute allocation sweeps are performed.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results left out. Figure 4 results are retained separately by model and downstream task; plotted values are recorded as figure only.

untested.parts: Not tested: the models are genomic, not text language models.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.

Power-law form, exponents and range over orders of magnitude are untested; only three sizes spanning about 9x with no fit. Image/video, repeated-data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes are also untested.
No comparison of fits or exponents across setups.

missing.what: Final-checkpoint probing scores of Botanic0-S/M/L compared across model size on five PlantCAD tasks. This bears on downstream scaling with size.
Fine-tuning scores of Botanic0-S/M/L on 17 PGB tasks; the size effect is unclear and the gap to AgroNT narrows.
Training longer gave only marginal final-loss gains, while downstream performance for L was not yet saturated.
Statement that improved likelihood correlated with stronger downstream performance in their benchmark.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is weak: three sizes, figure-only curves, no fits and no uncertainty. The validation set is out-of-distribution species. The LR schedule (inverse-sqrt decay, 315K horizon, stopped at ~150K) confounds loss-vs-step curves as a data-scaling measure.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits or exponents; no independent sweeps over parameters, tokens, and compute; no demonstration over several orders of magnitude.
No forecasts fitted on smaller runs and evaluated against substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests plant genomic MLM pretraining only; does not establish a power-law form or test image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes.
Reports downstream probing across pretraining steps, but does not fit a predictive relationship to pretraining loss or report downstream forecasts.
No comparison of fitted laws or exponents across setup or fitting choices.

relationships.reason: Held-out loss falls with steps and model size with no saturation (R2, R4, R6). This supports the direction only; no power-law form is shown.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out loss decreases with training steps and model size without saturation, although a power-law form is untested.

relationships.condition: XGBoost probing across pretraining checkpoints, six tasks, three sizes
relationships.reason: Downstream scores rise sharply over the first ~60K steps, then plateau or rise slowly. They are less smooth and less monotonic than loss (R7–R24).
relationships.display_finding: Downstream scores rose sharply during approximately the first 60K steps, then plateaued or increased slowly, with less smooth and less monotonic trajectories than loss.
